title: Uncontrolled information flow in class 3 rules hinders universality proofs

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Uncontrolled information flow in class 3 rules hinders universality proofs

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Universality proofs proceed by building components from localized structures, which requires controlled transmission of information; in class 3 systems a change to a single cell eventually spreads to all cells, making it very hard to identify definite components and hence to prove universality.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And this kind of uncontrolled transmission of information makes it very difficult to identify pieces that could be used as definite components in a construction.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 11, “The Notion of Computation”; section “The Threshold of Universality in Cellular Automata” (from p. 694), p. 698. Scope: class 3 cellular automata and methods for proving universality

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch11-23: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.43

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Damage spreading and localized structures are computable for finite samples. Existing analyses cannot cleanly establish that uncontrolled flow causes proof difficulty in general or excludes other proof methods.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure damage spreading from single-cell perturbations and compare the availability of persistent localized structures and proof constructions across classified rules. A strong association between spreading and failed component-based constructions would support this particular methodological mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Failure to find components does not imply none exist.

Proof difficulty is partly sociological and method-dependent.

Not every class 3 rule has identical perturbation dynamics.

fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.45

discriminating power: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The spreading clause is an ordinary simulation: one-cell perturbations of rules such as rule 30 can be measured and either stay localized or fill the light cone. The clause about proofs is methodological. Simulation can show that the usual glider-component route lacks stable pieces, without showing that no proof of any kind exists.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For agreed class-3 rules, flip one cell on a random background and measure the fraction of the light cone that eventually differs. Confirm uncontrolled spread if the difference reaches essentially the whole cone; the further claim that this makes component-style proofs very difficult is supported only as a record of which proof techniques succeed.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Very difficult is a judgment about proof search, and a later successful construction would not erase the historical difficulty.

Class 3 itself is a visual category, so membership of borderline rules is not unique.
